requirements.evidence: Entity.php:45-47 has a stray block causing a parse error; EntityInvite.php:12 uses HasFactory without importing it; Members.php:70-74 rejects every invite via `!RateLimiter::availableIn()`; Members.php:142/153/183 call `entity->members()` (a users relation, see Entity.php:49-50) as if it were memberships; PendingInvites.php:45 creates a User instead of a membership; members.blade.php:54 never shows the modal; lang files under resources/lang/ are missing nearly all required e-mail strings; the pending-invites component is never wired into onboarding or the switcher.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes (`sendInvite`, `accept`, `decline`, `saveRole`) live in Livewire components instead of `app/Actions/*` (Members.php:63-189, PendingInvites.php:30-63); authorization uses ad-hoc abilities `viewMembers`/`deleteInvite`/`deleteMember` (Members.php:54,136,184) with no policy; audit logging downgraded from `Log::channel('audit')` to `Log::info` (Members.php:118); no tests, no admin/onboarding views, no docs/CHANGELOG updates; dead imports throughout (factory:9 imports a non-existent `Carbon` facade).

security.evidence: `$entity` is no longer a declared `#[Locked]` property (Members.php:24-28) yet is assigned in mount (:48) and trusted by every action; `openMember`/`confirmRemoval`/`cancelRemoval` authorize nothing (Members.php:140-179); the members route has no manager guard and lost `current_entity`/`verified` middleware (routes/web.php:7-13); `saveRole` writes a client-supplied `memberRole` onto the wrong model (:165); gate abilities are undefined so authorization either 500s or is absent.

tests.evidence: The 13 changed files contain no test file at all (`grep '^diff --git' change.diff`); none of the required Livewire happy-path, validation, unauthorized-call or tamper tests, invite-expiry/duplicate tests, or mail-rendering tests were added.

simplicity.evidence: Duplicate hardcoded English labels and near-copied modal markup (members.blade.php:54-97 nests a second modal), an unused `$listeners` block (Members.php:30-32) and unused imports (Members.php:11,16; PendingInvites.php:6-11), while core logic that already existed (membership relations, manager counting, audit channel) was rewritten instead of reused.

readability.evidence: Methods such as `sendInvite` (Members.php:63-131) mix validation, rate limiting, duplicate checks, insert, mail and logging with running commentary; leftover reasoning like `// Set tenant session? Assuming tenant middleware will use entity` (PendingInvites.php:51) and `// assuming enum value` (EntityInviteMail.php:26); a junk language key in en.json:9; routes/web.php ends with `?>`.

scope.evidence: routes/web.php is replaced wholesale (14 lines left), deleting login, register, onboarding, switcher, settings, home, password reset, e-mail verification and entity pick routes, and adding a placeholder dashboard closure that returns a non-existent `entity.dashboard` view (routes/web.php:9-12) — a large unrelated regression.

issues.explanation: A stray anonymous block `{ return $this->hasMany(EntityMembership::class); }` was inserted after `invites()`, which is a PHP parse error in the class body and makes the whole application fail to load.

The route file was rewritten down to two routes, deleting login/register/onboarding/switcher/settings/password-reset/verification/home/pick routes and adding a placeholder dashboard closure, so the app is broken and `route('login')` used by the invite mail no longer exists.

The `#[Locked] public Entity $entity` declaration was removed but mount still does `$this->entity = $entity` and every method uses it; as an undeclared dynamic property it is not hydrated, so all actions after the first request see null.

One shared `$rules` array validates both forms, so `sendInvite()` fails on the required, initially empty `memberRole` and `saveRole()` fails on the required, initially empty `inviteEmail`; neither action can ever succeed.

`RateLimiter::availableIn()` returns 0 when the key has no hits, so `!RateLimiter::availableIn($key)` is always true and every invite is rejected with 'limit reached'; no 10-per-hour limit is actually implemented.

Member actions resolve `entity->members()`, which is the users relation (Entity.php:49-50), not memberships: `$membership->role->value` errors on a User, `saveRole` would write a role column onto users, and `removeMember` deletes the user instead of the membership.

The component switches to `App\Enums\UserRole` with lowercase cases while the contract and existing code use `App\Models\UserRole` with `Employee`/`Owner` cases, so the enum, `->value` calls and the cast in EntityInvite.php:24 likely resolve to a missing class.

Authorization relies on `viewMembers`, `deleteInvite` and `deleteMember` abilities, none of which are defined in the diff (no policy change), so managers get a 500 and employees are not explicitly 403'd as the task requires.
The entity context is no longer a `#[Locked]` public property, so the client can tamper with `entity` and point invite/role/removal actions at another entity; mount also performs no manager check.
`use HasFactory;` is used without importing `Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Factories\HasFactory`, causing a trait-not-found fatal error for the model and its factory.

Accepting an invite calls `members()->create([...])` on the users relation, which creates a User record with a `role` column instead of an EntityMembership; the required duplicate-membership guard and tenant session write are also missing (:51 is only a comment).

The member-detail modal is only `is-active` while `$confirmingRemoval` is true, so `openMember()` never shows it, and the removal confirmation modal is nested inside it rather than being a separate modal triggered by `confirmRemoval()`.

The mailable does not implement `ShouldQueue` and uses `build()->markdown()` instead of the contract's `content()->markdown`; the markdown view (resources/views/emails/entity-invite.blade.php:1) also wraps its body in `@component('mail::message')`, which is wrong for a markdown mailable.

Language files were created under `resources/lang/` instead of the required `lang/` path, and all the required e-mail/UI strings (greeting, 'as :role.', instruction, button, expiry, 'Team PegaFila', 'Invite member', 'Send invite', Accept/Decline) are missing; en.json:9 is a leftover note keyed as a translation.

The PendingInvites component is never included on the entity switcher or onboarding page (no view changes in the diff), so requirement 6 is entirely unmet; the heading and buttons are also hardcoded English instead of `ui.invites_title`/'Accept'/'Decline' keys.
Invite creation/acceptance/decline and role changes are domain writes and per conventions belong in `app/Actions/*` classes that authorize inside the action, not inline in Livewire components.
No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the change, so none of the new behavior, validation paths, expiry/idempotency rules, or the mandatory unauthorized-call and tamper tests exist.

`openMember`, `confirmRemoval` and `cancelRemoval` are public endpoints that perform no authorization at all, and `openMember` does not resolve a membership scoped to the entity as the requirement demands.
The members route lost `verified`/`current_entity` middleware and has no manager guard, so the route-level 403 for employees required by the task is absent.
The 'already a member' check goes through `User::whereHas('entities')` rather than the entity's memberships and does not normalize/case-fold the e-mail, so it can miss existing members.
The unique-constraint race path only recognises MySQL error 1062 on `errorInfo`; on SQLite/PostgreSQL the exception is rethrown as a 500 instead of an `inviteEmail` error.
The last-manager guard counts only `admin` rows (ignoring the owner), compares a string to the `UserRole::admin` enum so the branch is always taken, and therefore produces incorrect 403s.
`$existing->expires_at->isFuture()` dereferences a date that the migration makes nullable (migration:17), so a null expiry causes an error instead of being treated as expired.
The `role` enum permits `owner` even though owner is never invitable, and `expires_at` is nullable although every invite must be created with a 7-day expiry.
`invited_by` uses `cascadeOnDelete()`, so deleting a user silently destroys invite history, while the spec only calls for a nullable FK.
The audit entry uses `Log::info` instead of the project's `Log::channel('audit')`, which the removed code used and the logging conventions require.

The `<x-slot name="title">` and the component's `#[Layout('layouts::default-page')]` were removed, so the required page title 'Membros de :entity' is not set and the page is no longer rendered in the shared layout.
The pending-invites list filters only `accepted_at`, so expired invites are displayed as pending.
Unused imports (`User`, `UserRole`, `Gate`, `Log`, `Redirect`) and unresolved TODO-style comments ('Set tenant session? Assuming...') were left in production code.
Imports `Illuminate\Support\Facades\Carbon`, a class that does not exist, and never uses it.
Unused `Cache`/`Validator` imports and an unused `$listeners` refresh handler add noise.

review.summary: The change attempts the whole invite feature (model, migration, factory, mailable, two Livewire components, views, lang files) but does not run: Entity.php has a syntax error, EntityInvite is missing its HasFactory import, the undeclared `$entity` property is not hydrated, the rate limiter always rejects, and member actions query the users relation instead of memberships. It also rewrites routes/web.php into an app-breaking stub, leaves the modals unreachable, ships no tests, and never wires PendingInvites into onboarding or the switcher, so it must be rejected.
